meta.title: Check your understanding: The clean-energy system

objectives: Describe the three jobs every power system does: make, move and match
Explain how variety, time-shifting and reach help a grid built on wind and solar
Use the electricity-mix chart to compare how countries' sources of electricity have changed

questions.prompt: Why does a grid have to match supply to demand second by second?
choices: Because power stations are only allowed to run at full output
Because wind and solar can only be switched on during daylight
Because electricity prices are set again every second
Because a grid holds almost no energy of its own
questions.explain: A grid stores almost nothing, so at every moment the electricity going in must equal what comes out. Wind and solar make the matching harder, but the need existed long before them, when operators simply burned more or less fuel.

questions.prompt: A calm, cloudy region needs power on a winter evening, while a neighbouring country is windy. Which of the page's three ideas helps most?
choices: Reach: an interconnector lets the calm region import the windy country's power
Time-shifting: the region stores its own midday solar from the cloudy day
Variety: more solar panels in the calm region make up the evening shortfall
Variety: the calm region's own wind farms make up for the missing sun
questions.explain: Reach means long lines and interconnectors that carry energy from where it is plentiful to where it is needed, so a calm, cloudy place can import from a windy one. Storing midday solar does little on a cloudy day, and local solar or wind cannot help while the local sun and wind are missing.

questions.prompt: Hydrogen can store energy for weeks or months. What is its main drawback as a store of electricity, according to the system map?
choices: It can be kept for only a few hours before it leaks away
It is already the largest store of electricity, so it has little room left to grow
Well over half the energy is lost on the way back to electricity
It responds too slowly to count as a form of storage
questions.explain: Turning electricity into hydrogen and back loses well over half the energy: that is the price of storing it for weeks or months. The largest store of electricity today is pumped hydro, and it is batteries that typically hold only a few hours.

questions.prompt: Net load is demand minus wind and solar. At 6 pm a grid's demand is 30 GW, wind makes 6 GW and solar 2 GW. What net load must everything else supply?
questions.explain: Net load is what remains after wind and solar: 30 − 6 − 2 = 22 GW must come from hydro, storage, other plants or imports. 8 GW is the wind and solar output itself, and 38 GW comes from adding them to demand instead of subtracting.
